# Caption-then-index with a vision LLM

*Notebooks: [`02a_multimodal_rag_with_captioning.ipynb`](https://github.com/Sourav692/rag-agents-engineering/blob/main/course/p07_rag_applications/m21_multimodal_rag/notebooks/02a_multimodal_rag_with_captioning.ipynb)*

## Captioning

Captioning moves the vision work to index time. A vision model looks at each figure once and writes text about it, and from then on the figure is a text chunk: the same embedder, the same vector store and the same retriever as the paragraphs around it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I[/"Figure image"/] --> V["Vision LLM<br/>caption prompt"]
    V --> C["Caption text"]
    C --> E["Text embedder"]
    E --> X[("Index<br/>chunks and captions")]
    Q[/Question/] --> E2["Same embedder"]
    E2 --> X
```

The notebook builds it on the Attention paper (`1706.03762v7.pdf`):

1. **Extract.** PyMuPDF reads each page's text into one Document per page and saves every embedded image to `extracted_images/`.
2. **Caption.** `gemini-1.5-flash`, through `google.generativeai`, gets each image with the prompt *"You are an assistant tasked with summarising tables, images and text for retrieval. These summaries will be embedded and used to retrieve the raw text or table elements. Give a concise summary of the table or text that is well optimised for retrieval."*
3. **Index.** Page texts and captions both go through `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.from_tiktoken_encoder(chunk_size=400, chunk_overlap=50)`, are embedded with Cohere `embed-english-v3.0`, and share one Chroma collection.
4. **Answer.** The retriever returns `k = 1` item, and `command-r-plus` at temperature 0 answers from it.

The cost lands once per image, at index time, and never per question. The index holds only text, so every tool from [M14](/learn/ingestion-and-indexing-pipeline/embeddings-and-model-selection/embeddings-and-model-selection-overview) to [M19](/learn/retrieval-quality-engineering/post-retrieval-optimisation-and-reranking/post-retrieval-optimisation-and-reranking-overview) still applies to captions: hybrid search, reranking, metadata filters.

The test question in the notebook never reaches a caption. PyMuPDF finds three raster images in the paper: Figure 1 on page 3 and the two images that make up Figure 2 on page 4. Figures 3 to 5 are not stored as images, so `get_images()` returns nothing for them. *What is the BLEU score of the Transformer (base model)?* is answered by Table 2 on page 8, which is text. `get_text()` returns it with the rows flattened, one cell per line (`Transformer (base model)`, `27.3`, `38.1`, `3.3 · 1018`), and the training cost 3.3 × 10^18 comes out as "1018". The notebook's system prompt also says *"Answer the question based upon your knowledge"*, which invites the model to answer from memory rather than from the retrieved chunk. To test captioning, ask about something only a figure shows.

On the Larkspur pages the [interactive lab](/labs/rag/m21_multimodal_rag/chart-retrieval-lab.html) embeds the captions with `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, the same model as the text chunks. The captions are representative, written the way a vision model following the notebook's prompt would write them. Captions rank 2, 1 and 1 for the three questions. The first misses at `k = 1` because the paragraph *"Figure 1 shows monthly availability for April, May and June against the 99.95% target"* repeats the question's words and scores 0.747, against 0.693 for the caption. Captions compete with text chunks on one scale, so the ranking is fair, and a `k` of 2 or 3 sends both.

## What a caption must hold

The notebook's prompt asks for a summary "well optimised for retrieval". Retrieval needs less than the answer does. With a short caption that names the chart and leaves out the values, such as *"Bar chart of monthly availability in Q2 against a target line."*, the lab's embedder still ranks it 2, 3 and 2 for the three questions. It is found, and it cannot answer: nothing in it says May or 99.91%.

Write the caption prompt for the questions the figure must answer:

- **Every printed value**, with its label and unit: "April 99.98%, May 99.91%, June 99.97%".
- **The title, axes and legend**, and any reference line ("a dashed line marks the 99.95% target").
- **The figure's place**: document, page, figure number, so a citation can point at it.
- **An explicit escape** for anything unreadable, as [M06](/learn/prompt-and-context-engineering/multimodal-prompting/multimodal-prompting-overview) does with `[NOT_EXTRACTED]`, so the captioner leaves a gap instead of guessing.

A caption is model output, written once and then trusted on every query. If the vision model reads 8 GB as 16 GB, retrieval will find the wrong number with full confidence. The notebook already keeps the image file name in each caption's metadata (`name`), which is enough to retrieve on the caption and then send the original image to a vision model at answer time. The caption then only has to be good enough to find the figure. Where a PDF has a real text layer, an element-level parser that returns each table as HTML ([M12, lesson 12.4](/learn/ingestion-and-indexing-pipeline/document-ingestion-and-metadata-design/pdf-and-word-parser-comparison-and-element-level-parsing)) keeps rows and columns that a caption has to describe in prose.
